bio.title: Meet Rudolph
bio.description: Learn about Rudolph "Rudy" Tinker's background, service, and commitment to Palm Beach County District 6.
bio.content:
Rudolph "Rudy" Tinker is a U.S. Army veteran, Certified General Contractor, small business owner, and educator who has lived, worked, and raised his family in Palm Beach County District 6 for more than two decades.

He believes government should work for everyday people—not insiders, not special interests.

Rudy was raised by a devoted single mother and grandmother in a close, multigenerational household. From an early age, he learned the values of faith, discipline, hard work, and service to others—values that continue to guide his life and leadership today.

Growing up in South Florida, Rudy became deeply connected to his community. He volunteered regularly, participated in neighborhood cleanups and food drives, supported crime-prevention efforts, and joined the Hallandale Police Explorer Program. For Rudy, service was never a slogan—it was simply how you showed up.

After graduating high school in 1996, Rudy enrolled at Florida Atlantic University. While initially pursuing medicine, he worked multiple jobs to put himself through school. Along the way, he discovered his passion for Political Science, realizing that the decisions made in government affect every family, every neighborhood, and every opportunity. During this time, he also started a small retail business in Palm Beach County, gaining firsthand experience with the challenges small business owners face.

In 2001, Rudy was hand-selected as a Congressional Intern for Congressman Alcee Hastings, representing the office at civic and community events during the difficult months following the September 11th attacks. That same year, he graduated from college, married young, and answered the call to serve—enlisting in the United States Army.

Rudy served honorably from 2002 to 2005 in support of the Global War on Terror. While on active duty, he purchased his first home in Loxahatchee in 2003—the community he has proudly called home ever since.

After returning to civilian life, Rudy became a father to triplets. Life soon brought unexpected hardship when one of his children passed away following a long battle with serious medical complications. For years, his life revolved around hospitals, emergency visits, and caring for children with complex needs—all while being the sole provider for his family.

Those experiences left a lasting mark. They taught Rudy what it truly means to fight for stability, affordability, and opportunity—and why leadership must be rooted in empathy and real-world experience, not theory.

Today, Rudy is married and raising his children in Loxahatchee. He owns and operates a construction and consulting firm that works directly in neighborhoods across District 6. His days are spent on job sites dealing with permitting delays, zoning issues, drainage and infrastructure problems, rising insurance costs, and housing affordability—seeing firsthand how county decisions affect working families, farmers, and small businesses.

Rudy is also an educator, teaching American Government at Palm Beach State College’s Loxahatchee and Belle Glade campuses. He has taught at Pahokee Middle–Senior High School and Glades Central High School, working closely with students and families throughout the Glades and western communities.

In the classroom, Rudy teaches the Constitution, the Bill of Rights, voting rights, and how local government decisions—from zoning and budgeting to property taxes and public services—directly shape people’s daily lives.

After decades of service—as a veteran, husband, father, contractor, educator, and community member—Rudy is running for public office because he knows District 6 deserves leadership that listens, shows up, plans responsibly, and puts people first.

Rudolph “Rudy” Tinker is not a career politician.

He is one of us—working for all of us.

whyIWantToRun.title: Why I'm Running for District 6
whyIWantToRun.description: Rudolph Tinker explains why he's running for Palm Beach County Commission District 6.
whyIWantToRun.content:
I'm running for Palm Beach County Commission District 6 because county government has lost touch with reality — and everyday people are paying the price.

For starters - property taxes keep going up with little to show for it.

Even worse, affordability continues to be out of reach for many residents – which has to stop!

And families are being squeezed for every penny, while seemingly county administrators waste money and protect themselves instead of the public.

In fact, according to the Florida Chief Financial Officer, Palm Beach County has been flagged for more than $344 million in wasteful or questionable spending. That's not politics — that's taxpayer money that could have gone toward lower property taxes, fixing roads, improving drainage, easing traffic, and finally investing in communities that have been ignored for decades!

Instead, residents are told there is "no money." This translates to over inflating public budgets without being held accountable.

And here is the INSULT!

All seven Palm Beach County Commissioners unanimously approved the $3.3 million security contract with the Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office (PBSO) on November 4, 2025. When you divide that number by seven commissioners, that comes out to about $471,000 per commissioner — more than four times a commissioner's annual salary.

LET THAT SINK IN!

At a time when homeowners are struggling, taxes are rising, and communities are being told to accept less, politicians are spending over 400% of their salary on taxpayer-funded security details!

What a shame!

I want to be clear: I will not accept a taxpayer-funded security detail like that – ever!

Public service is not about insulating yourself from the people you serve. You should not be in public office if you are unavailable to the people you serve.

Even worse is that while politicians protect themselves, communities like Loxahatchee Groves are losing law enforcement services because of the high cost of policing contracts.

Families are told there aren't enough resources — but somehow there's always money to protect elected officials.

That's not leadership!

That's privilege!

And decisions like these and many other wasteful spending endeavors need to end today!

As a licensed general contractor, I see firsthand how poor planning and bad county decisions raise costs for everyone. As a veteran, who served honorably in the United States Army, I know leadership means accountability, responsibility, and service — not ego! And as an educator, I teach people how government is supposed to work, because informed communities demand better government.

You should know - I'm not running to protect the status quo!

I'm running to change how our County does business!

Enough waste!

Enough neglect!

Enough with politicians protecting themselves while Palm Beach County families struggle!

Every Palm Beach County community deserves to be heard. Every Palm Beach County community deserves RESPECT. And every decision should be made with the people who live with it in mind.

I'm running because District 6 deserves REAL leadership that listens, plans responsibly, spends wisely, and shows up to work!

I am Rudolph "Rudy" Tinker!

One of us — Working for all of us!

Vote Rudy for District 6!

district6.title: District 6
district6.description: Learn about Palm Beach County District 6 and the role of a County Commissioner.
district6.headerTitle: About Palm Beach County Commission District 6
district6.content:
Palm Beach County's 6th Commission District is one of the largest and most diverse districts in Florida. Spanning roughly 1,300 square miles, District 6 stretches from the western communities along Lake Okeechobee to the rapidly growing central and western suburbs of Palm Beach County.

District 6 includes Royal Palm Beach, Loxahatchee Groves, The Acreage, Wellington, Westlake, Belle Glade, South Bay, Pahokee, and western portions of Lake Worth, along with vast areas of unincorporated Palm Beach County. As shown in the map, the district covers a large contiguous area, with a significant concentration of rural and agricultural land.

Importantly, District 6 encompasses the largest agricultural region east of the Mississippi River, producing winter vegetables that supply food across Florida and the nation. This unique mix of agricultural communities, rural neighborhoods, and fast-growing suburban areas makes District 6 unlike any other district in Palm Beach County.

What Does a Palm Beach County Commissioner Do?

The Palm Beach County Board of County Commissioners (BCC) is the county's primary legislative and policy-making body. Commissioners are responsible for setting countywide priorities and making decisions that directly affect residents' daily lives.

County Commissioners:

  • Enact countywide ordinances and policies
  • Approve the county budget and authorize all expenditures of county funds
  • Oversee major public services and infrastructure projects

In addition, the Board of County Commissioners also serves as:

  • The Governing Board of the Solid Waste Authority
  • The Environmental Control Board
  • The Zoning Board for unincorporated Palm Beach County

This means commissioners have direct influence over taxes, waste collection, environmental protections, land use, zoning, infrastructure, and public services—especially in unincorporated areas like much of District 6.

How the Board Is Elected

Palm Beach County is represented by seven County Commissioners, each elected from a single-member district to staggered four-year terms.

  • Districts 2, 4, and 6 appear on the gubernatorial election ballot
  • Districts 1, 3, 5, and 7 appear on the presidential election ballot

The Board of County Commissioners typically meets on the first and third Tuesday of each month to conduct public hearings and vote on agenda items affecting the entire county.

service.title: A Legacy of Service
service.subtitle: Rudolph Tinker’s Army Journey
service.content:
Rudolph "Rudy" Tinker enlisted in the United States Army in 2002, driven by a deep sense of duty following the events of September 11th. Serving honorably from 2002 to 2005 during the Global War on Terror, Rudy learned the true meaning of leadership, discipline, and sacrifice.

His service wasn't just about the uniform; it was about protecting the values we hold dear and ensuring that those who serve our country are never forgotten when they return home. Today, he brings that same mission-driven focus to his campaign for County Commission.

va.title: Palm Beach County VA
va.subtitle: Supporting Our Heroes Locally
va.content:
The West Palm Beach VA Medical Center is a lifeline for thousands of veterans in our community. Rudy believes that local government must play a proactive role in partnering with the VA to ensure veterans have seamless access to healthcare, mental health resources, and housing assistance.

As your Commissioner, Rudy will advocate for expanded transportation options for veterans to reach the VA and push for local initiatives that bridge the gap between federal benefits and local needs.

sections.heading: Tax
bullets: Provide a 100% county property tax exemption for homestead property owners age 65 and over who have maintained Palm Beach County residency and paid property taxes for at least 15 consecutive years.
Twenty-five years paid. No more county property taxes.
Long-term Palm Beach County homeowners deserve real relief.
Freeze county property tax rates and implement annual rollbacks funded by eliminating wasteful county spending, prioritizing efficiency, audits, and administrative cost reductions.

sections.heading: Delinquent Tax
bullets: Allow Any payment method for late property tax.
Delay tax certificate sales until July of the delinquent year.
Increase early payment discount from 4% to 10%.
Reduce delinquent interest from 18% to 9%
Extend Tax Deed application from 2 years to 5 years on homestead homes.

sections.heading: Building Department
bullets: Your roof protects your family. Five days. Period. No homeowner waits weeks or months for a roof permit.

sections.heading: Code Enforcement
bullets: Code enforcement has become legalized harassment.
If code enforcement can’t prove a real health or safety risk, they won’t fine you. Period
Cap & Eliminate Excessive Fines
Daily fines on homesteads will be capped and abolished where abusive.
Zero Selective Enforcement
Same rules, same treatment—no targeting by neighborhood, income, or politics
Stop importing bureaucrats. Hire locals who live in the community and understand how people actually live.
We’re shifting from Code Enforcement to Community Compliance & Assistance—focused on fixing problems, not punishing people.

sections.heading: Building Department
bullets: Service, Not Obstruction
The Building Department exists to help projects move safely and legally—not to delay, intimidate, or over-complicate approvals.
Fast-Track for Minor & Residential Work
Establish guaranteed turnaround times for residential permits, repairs, and small projects—no months-long delays for basic work.
Right to Challenge Without Retaliation
Contractors and homeowners may appeal decisions without fear of blacklisting, delays, or targeted enforcement.
Automatic Amnesty for Old Permits

Any inactive permit 10, 20, or 30 years old on a property where Palm Beach County has continuously collected property taxes shall be administratively closed without penalty. You can’t tax a property for decades and then pretend the work never existed. Close the permit. Move on.
No Punishment for New Homeowners
Buyers will not be fined or penalized for permit issues created by prior owners. Responsibility follows the violator—not the victim.
Your roof protects your family.
Five days. Period. No homeowner waits weeks or months for a roof permit.

sections.heading: Agriculture Exemption Department
bullets: If your land is zoned Residential Ag and you qualify, you get the exemption. No more games. No more denial.
If land is zoned for agriculture and is being used for any legitimate agricultural purpose, it qualifies. Letting land rest and grow is still land management, not neglect.
Intent Matters
Agricultural use includes preparation, recovery, rotation, and land conditioning—not just harvest.
If your land can reasonably support the animal with proper management, one cow can qualify—especially on residential-ag or small farm parcels.

sections.heading: Idle time creates problems. Opportunity builds futures.
bullets: Give kids something to do, somewhere to go, and a future to build—right here in our western communities.
Community gyms & rec centers
Aqua center
Motor Sports
BMX Park

sections.heading: Affordable, Healthy Housing
bullets: Safe, affordable housing and improved maintenance of existing neighborhoods are priorities, especially where poverty is high.

sections.heading: Respect the Glades Voice
bullets: Ensure the Glades has a real seat at the table—fair county funding, representation, and follow-through, not election-season visits.
Major county decisions must include direct input from Glades residents.

sections.heading: Infrastructure Repair & Services
bullets: Better roads, drainage, utilities, and public services are repeatedly cited as needed improvements that would make living conditions safer and fairer.

sections.heading: Clear Air and Water
bullets: Protect Glades communities from smoke, burning, and industrial air pollution that harms health.
Ensure clean drinking water and protect canals, wells, and Lake Okeechobee from contamination.

sections.heading: Fix Roads & Potholes
bullets: Resurface unsafe roads and prioritize rural and Glades areas that have been ignored.

sections.heading: Inadequate Drainage & Flooding
bullets: I will push for regular canal maintenance, improved culverts, and real flood control—not excuses.

sections.heading: Address Traffic & Growth Impacts
bullets: I will demand road improvements keep pace with development to reduce congestion and accidents.

sections.heading: Existing Road Projects in district 6
bullets: End road project delays in District 6. Get construction moving, fix unsafe roads, and relieve traffic congestion—now, not later.

sections.heading: Overdevelopment

Put rural residents first—listen to them and respect how they want their neighborhoods preserved.

sections.heading: Community Policing in Every Neighborhood
